articles.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Blurs Into a Cloud of Drudgery
articles.summary: Just when you think there’s no more life in a franchise, an executive somewhere puts a crowbar in the crypt and revives an old moneymaker for one more round. The first four Hunger Games movies, released from 2012 to 2015 and adapted from Suzanne Collins’ enormously successful young-adult novels , featured Jennifer Lawrence as the ever-plucky Katniss Everdeen. She gave those movies a bristling vitality that could keep you watching even if you had no interest in the material's hyper-dramatic teen dystopian visions .

articles.title: Here Are the Senators Who Are Backing Van Hollen Over Schumer for Senate Majority Leader
articles.summary: Senator Chris Van Hollen has said that he has the backing of about 15 of his colleagues in his quest to challenge Senator Chuck Schumer for Senate Majority Leader. So far, only a few of them have publicly declared their support. articles.title: Muslims Are Projected to Become the World’s Largest Religious Group by 2035, Surpassing Christians. Here’s Why
articles.summary: Muslims are projected to become the world’s largest religious group —overtaking Christians , who have long held that distinction—by 2035. And the gap between the two populations is set to keep steadily widening in the ensuing decades if recent trends continue, with Muslims potentially representing 3.64 billion people around the globe in 2070 compared to 2.96 billion Christians. articles.title: Scientists Are Pursuing the Dream of a 'Virtual Cell'
articles.summary: A single cell is a world unto itself, billions of interlocking molecules whose intricate patterns foretell health and disease. Biologists usually investigate how cells work in the lab. But in recent years, the idea of a “virtual cell” —a computer model so detailed, with such a close resemblance to the real thing, that scientists could run experiments on it instead of in the lab—has entered the conversation . articles.title: In Elsinore, a Radiant Andrew Scott Finds Life in a Play About Death
articles.summary: Contracting HIV is no longer a death sentence. But before the current medications and treatments emerged, the AIDS crisis of the 1980s and 1990s touched almost everyone, gay or straight, whether you wanted to admit it or not. Friends of friends, acquaintances or associates who brightened your day, or, worst of all, a loved one: people you cherished could wither and disappear in practically a heartbeat.
